title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia Etc vs State Of Punjab on 9 April, 1980
judges_list: Bench: Y.V. Chandrachud, P.N. Bhagwati, N.L. Untwalia, R.S. Pathak, O. Chinnappa Reddy
acts_list: Section 46 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not contemplate any formality before a person can be said to be taken in custody

sections_structured.act: the Evidence Act in regard to a discovery of facts made in pursuance of information supplied by a person released on bail by invoking the principle stated by this Court in State of U.P. v. Deoman Upadhyaya to the effect that when a person not in custody approaches a police officer investigating an offence and offers to give information leading to the discovery of a fact
the Evidence Act can be made out

outcome_summary: The court holds that granting blanket anticipatory bail is not appropriate and orders should specify the offence or offences for which the bail applies.
conclusion_clean: bail" to an accused who is under arrest involves a contradiction in terms, in so far as the offence or offences for which he is arrested, are concerned.
plain_summary: The court holds that granting blanket anticipatory bail is not appropriate and orders should specify the offence or offences for which the bail applies. The court also emphasizes the importance of specifying conditions in anticipatory bail orders.
key_reasons: Reason to believe must be founded on reasonable grounds
Specific events and facts must be disclosed by the applicant
Order should specify the offence or offences
conditions: Condition that the person shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required
Condition that the person shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case
Condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court
